propositions.text: Applicant Singh seeks judicial review of Officer's January 5, 2021 decision refusing permanent residence on H&C grounds under IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant Singh seeks judicial review of Officer's January 5, 2021 decision refusing permanent residence on H&C grounds under IRPA, court states.

propositions.text: Officer's decision is unreasonable, erred in analyzing hardship upon return to Singapore and evidence assessment.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues Officer's decision is unreasonable due to errors in hardship analysis and evidence assessment.

propositions.text: Officer's decision is unreasonable; judicial review application allowed.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds Officer's decision unreasonable and allows judicial review application.

propositions.text: Applicant is 43-year-old Singapore citizen with cerebral palsy causing significant physical limitations and requiring a walker.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant is a 43-year-old Singapore citizen with cerebral palsy and significant physical limitations, court states.

propositions.text: Applicant's immediate family immigrated to Canada; brother is Canadian citizen who sponsored mother; Applicant visited Canada in 2017.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant's family immigrated to Canada; brother sponsored mother; Applicant visited Canada in 2017, court states.

propositions.text: Applicant lives with family in Canada, supported by mother and brother; no support system in Singapore; father deceased.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant lives with family in Canada, supported by mother and brother, with no support in Singapore; father deceased, court states.

propositions.text: Applicant submitted permanent residence application on H&C grounds on September 4, 2019.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant submitted permanent residence application on H&C grounds on September 4, 2019, court states.

propositions.text: Officer refused Applicant's H&C application on January 5, 2021, finding insufficient H&C considerations.

paragraphs.summary: Officer refused Applicant's H&C application on January 5, 2021 due to insufficient H&C considerations, court reports.

propositions.text: Officer gave modest weight to Applicant's establishment in Canada but noted little integration and long absences.

paragraphs.summary: Officer gave modest weight to Applicant's establishment but noted little integration and long absences, court reports.

propositions.text: Officer accepted discrimination against disabled in Singapore but found no personal discrimination shown by Applicant; noted Singapore's redress steps reducing hardship.

paragraphs.summary: Officer accepted discrimination in Singapore but found no personal discrimination by Applicant; noted redress steps reducing hardship, court reports.

propositions.text: Officer acknowledged Applicant's cerebral palsy and family support but found unclear support needs and questioned paternal family support in Singapore; gave some weight to separation hardship.

paragraphs.summary: Officer acknowledged Applicant's condition and support but found unclear needs and questioned Singapore family support; gave some weight to separation hardship, court reports.

propositions.text: Sole issue is whether Officer's decision is reasonable.

paragraphs.summary: Court states sole issue is whether Officer's decision is reasonable.

propositions.text: Both parties agree and court concurs that reasonableness is the standard of review for H&C decisions, citing cases.

paragraphs.summary: Court states parties agree and it concurs that reasonableness is the review standard for H&C decisions, citing authorities.

propositions.text: Reasonableness is deferential but robust; decision must be transparent, intelligible, justified, coherent, and rational per Vavilov.

paragraphs.summary: Court explains reasonableness standard requires transparent, intelligible, justified, coherent, and rational decision per Vavilov.

propositions.text: Unreasonableness requires central flaws; court must not reweigh evidence or interfere absent exceptional circumstances; flaws must be more than minor.

paragraphs.summary: Court states unreasonableness requires central flaws; no reweighing or interference absent exceptional circumstances; flaws must be significant.

propositions.text: Under IRPA s 25(1), Minister may grant permanent residence on H&C grounds including BIOC considerations.

paragraphs.summary: Court states IRPA s 25(1) allows permanent residence on H&C grounds including best interests of child considerations.

propositions.text: Officer accepted evidence of discrimination and stigma against disabled in Singapore but found Applicant did not show personal discrimination.

paragraphs.summary: Officer accepted discrimination evidence but found Applicant did not show personal discrimination, court reports.

propositions.text: Applicant says he provided objective evidence of discrimination and impact on his life; Officer failed to engage with his specific circumstances.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues he provided evidence of discrimination and impact; Officer failed to engage with his circumstances.

propositions.text: Applicant argues he need not show personal discrimination, relying on Miyir and other cases rejecting personalized risk in H&C analysis.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues no need to show personal discrimination, citing Miyir and cases rejecting personalized risk in H&C.

propositions.text: Applicant cites Caleb and Kanthasamy confirming H&C applicants need not show personal targeting; country conditions relevant even if general.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant cites Caleb and Kanthasamy confirming no personal targeting needed; general country conditions relevant in H&C.

propositions.text: Onus was on Applicant to provide sufficient evidence of hardship for H&C exemption
Officer reasonably found insufficient information about Applicant's personal experiences in Singapore
Nicayenzi v Canada and Kisana v Canada cited for onus and evidence standards

paragraphs.summary: Respondent argues Applicant bore onus to prove hardship for H&C exemption; Officer reasonably found insufficient evidence, citing Nicayenzi and Kisana.

propositions.text: Applicant provided few specific examples of daily life in Singapore without family
Applicant must link personal circumstances to country conditions showing direct negative impact
Singh, Khalifa, and Pierre cases cited for linking personal circumstances to country conditions

paragraphs.summary: Respondent submits Applicant gave few examples of daily life and must link circumstances to country conditions, citing Singh, Khalifa, and Pierre.

propositions.text: Disagrees with Respondent's reliance on pre-Kanthasamy case law
Kanthasamy allows inferences from discrimination against others sharing identity; no need to prove personal targeting

paragraphs.summary: Court disagrees with Respondent's pre-Kanthasamy case reliance; Kanthasamy allows inferences from discrimination without personal targeting proof.

propositions.text: Applicant's submissions tie his disability and circumstances to discrimination faced in Singapore
Finds Applicant's submissions do tie personal circumstances to discrimination faced by disabled in Singapore
Officer erred by requiring Applicant to show personal effect of discrimination
Kanthasamy and post-Kanthasamy jurisprudence require less personal evidence of discrimination

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues and court finds submissions tie disability to discrimination; Officer erred requiring personal effect proof per Kanthasamy.

propositions.text: Officer failed to assess adequacy of Singapore's state protection for disabled
Officer wrongly relied on Singapore government's efforts to reduce hardship
Officer found availability of redress reduces hardship for disabled in Singapore

paragraphs.summary: Applicant submits Officer failed to assess adequacy of Singapore's protection and wrongly relied on government efforts reducing hardship.

propositions.text: Agrees with Applicant that legislation or initiatives do not prove adequate protection or improved conditions
Ramesh and Ocampo cases require assessing actual impact of government efforts, not just efforts themselves

paragraphs.summary: Court agrees legislation alone doesn't prove protection; cites Ramesh and Ocampo requiring assessment of actual impact.

propositions.text: Officer committed reviewable errors making hardship analysis unreasonable

paragraphs.summary: Court finds Officer made reviewable errors rendering hardship analysis unreasonable.

propositions.text: Kanthasamy defines H&C considerations as facts evoking desire to relieve misfortune
Officer focused only on hardship, not full H&C factors as required by Chirwa and Kanthasamy
Chirwa, Kanthasamy, Marshall, and Lobjanidze require holistic H&C analysis

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues Officer focused only on hardship, not full H&C factors as required by Chirwa and Kanthasamy jurisprudence.

propositions.text: Officer illogically concluded no evidence of needed family assistance and speculated about extended family support
Officer questioned what support Applicant needs and why paternal relatives can't help, citing lack of evidence

paragraphs.summary: Applicant alleges Officer illogically found no evidence of needed family support and speculated about paternal relatives' help.

propositions.text: Officer's conclusion unsupported given medical evidence showing Applicant's limitations and need for family support
2019 doctor's letter confirms Applicant requires support and supervision from family

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues Officer's conclusion unsupported by medical evidence confirming need for family support.

propositions.text: Officer failed to consider family reunification and essential support in Canada for Applicant's disability
Salde requires H&C officers to consider all compassionate factors including family reunification

paragraphs.summary: Applicant submits Officer failed to consider family reunification; Salde requires considering all compassionate factors.

propositions.text: Reasonable decision makers may differ applying Kanthasamy's subjective H&C analysis to same evidence
Zlotosz supports that different conclusions can be reasonable under Kanthasamy

paragraphs.summary: Respondent argues reasonable decision makers may differ under Kanthasamy; cites Zlotosz.

propositions.text: 2019 doctor’s letter lacks detail on Applicant’s current health and specific assistance needed
Officer reasonably questioned what support Applicant needs and why paternal relatives can't provide it
Officer's questions about paternal relatives are logical, not speculative, due to lack of evidence

paragraphs.summary: Respondent submits doctor’s letter lacks detail; Officer reasonably questioned support needs and paternal relatives' role.

propositions.text: Evidence shows Applicant has cerebral palsy affecting daily activities and self-support
Applicant is highly dependent on mother and brother in Canada and lacks support system in Singapore

paragraphs.summary: Court finds Applicant has cerebral palsy, depends on family in Canada, and lacks support in Singapore.

propositions.text: Applicant states he is highly dependent on family in Canada and has no support in Singapore
Applicant’s mother states she cannot leave Canada because of disabled son in Singapore without care
Applicant’s brother states Applicant cannot live alone without family support in Canada

paragraphs.summary: Applicant and family statements confirm Applicant's dependency on family in Canada and lack of support in Singapore.

propositions.text: Officer did not adequately consider specific support role of Applicant’s mother and brother
Long-term family support cannot be replaced by hypothetical paternal family support without evidence

paragraphs.summary: Court finds Officer failed to consider family support role and wrongly presumed paternal family support without evidence.

propositions.text: Officer did not conduct holistic H&C analysis as required by Kanthasamy
Officer failed to consider compassionate elements including dependency and hardship without family support
Decision cannot stand

paragraphs.summary: Court concludes Officer failed holistic H&C analysis and compassionate considerations; decision cannot stand.

propositions.text: Officer’s decision failed to account for hardship from disability and family separation
Officer’s decision is unreasonable
Application for judicial review allowed; decision set aside; matter referred for redetermination by different officer
No questions for certification arise

paragraphs.summary: Court finds Officer’s decision unreasonable for failing to account hardship; allows review, sets aside decision, and refers matter back.
